serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText:
You: Unlike the last story, this one happened for real.
Bot: I hope you are not lying like last time…
You: Of course not! I wouldn’t do that!
You: I actually know a person involved in this story.
It’s a made up story, but it wouldn’t be fun if she knew that.
You: Story begins shortly after a young woman named Lucy received her grandfather’s house as inheritance after he died.
You: She was his only living relative since her parents died in an accident a few years prior.
You: Lucy didn’t know her grandfather very well, but from what her father told her, he was a horrible man and a huge misogynist.
You: He would not allow any woman to come to his home, not even his yard. Whenever he saw any woman nearby he would start screaming and yelling. 
You: The only time she saw him was at her parents' funeral, but he left as soon as the ceremony was over.
You: She felt nothing when she received the message that he died in his sleep. He was a complete stranger to her.
You: In his testament he wrote that after his death all of his possessions are to be given to the closest male relative, but since he didn’t have one, Lucy got everything.
You: ‘What a piece of shit’, she thought.
You: She decided to rent a car and ride to her grandfather’s house in the middle of nowhere to assess how much she could get from selling it.
You: She still got her college debt and getting some money would help a lot in the current economy.
You: The ride was long and when she finally got there it was late afternoon. It was a warm, summer day, but she was wondering if it would get cold at night.
You: It was a desolate place, but she could see a dirt road going further into the unknown. Could there be something more than her grandfather’s home?
You: For the moment she decided to go inside and see if there were any valuables as the house’s location left no hope of getting any buck out of it.
You: She felt disgusted at the sight of the conditions in which her grandfather lived.
You: House was full of trash and very dusty. She felt a little bad about her grandpa since it seemed like he might have been a victim of some untreated mental illness.
You: After a while she found a dirty, smelly armchair. It was probably where her grandfather died since it was the only place that wasn’t covered in dust.
You: Next to the armchair was laying a shotgun. It was shiny and obviously the only thing that was taken care of here.
You: ‘Uwah… {{wi}}He was seriously dangerous…’ she thought.
You: She was confused as to why it was left and not taken along with the body, but decided to continue her search.
You: After a while she found nothing of value. The only thing that caught her attention was a picture hanging on the wall. It was covered up by a pile of rusty items she didn’t know how to describe, but she finally got her hand on it.
You: It was an old family picture. She barely could recognize her father and grandfather. Standing next to them was some old man with a long beard. Maybe her grandfather?
You: While she was mesmerized by the picture…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.Shock
You: …a loud shriek could be heard outside!{{punch}}
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.Sad
You: It frightened Lucy so much that she dropped the picture which resulted in breaking the glass of the frame.
You: She stood there silently, full of fear. Trying to deduce what has just happened.
You: Was it her imagination? Surely not. It was too real.
You: After a while she heard another shriek, but this time it was much quieter.
You: It sounded like…{{wi}} crying of a little baby…
You: She couldn’t believe it, she was in the middle of nowhere after all, but she couldn’t deny what she was hearing. She had to go outside and investigate, but the whole situation was giving her the creeps.
You: For a second she thought about taking the gun with her, but she quickly discarded that idea. After all, she never held a gun in her life.
You: She gathered her courage and went outside while making sure to walk as silently as possible.
You: The source of the crying was located on the dirt road she was interested in before. There was an old baby carriage in the middle of it. 
You: ‘Who would leave a baby in a place like this’ crossed her mind, but she couldn’t just leave a baby alone like this.
You: She came up to the carriage and saw inside a newborn baby, crying at the top of its lungs.
You: Did the mother abandon it here for her to find? After all, the car she rented can be easily spotted.
You: ‘Fuck this’ said Lucy as she decided to find the mother as soon as possible. She had no way of transporting this baby safely to the nearest city.
You: It was already dark, but Lucy was pushing the carriage further down the dirt road. She walked and walked while the baby cried, but after an hour or so she saw a small village ahead of her.
You: Someone was clearly living there since a few lights were shining through the windows.
You: As she was getting closer, she heard a voice coming out from behind her.
You: Oh my! A young mother! You must be proud! The voice said.
You: Lucy almost jumped from surprise, but she controlled herself when she turned around and saw an old lady.
You: O-Oh, hi. Actually, it’s not my baby. I found it near my grandfather’s home. Lucy replied.
You:It’s not your baby? The old lady quickly responded.
Lucy: Yes. I was at my grandfather’s house. His name was Richarlison. I’m sure you knew him, he was living only an hour from here.
Lucy: Someone left this baby carriage with this newborn inside outside of my grandfather’s house. Do you know who might be the mother?
Old Lady: I don’t understand.
You: ‘Are you kidding me’? Thought Lucy. There was no one else nearby, that old hag had to know something.
Old Lady: What newborn are you talking about? I’m confused.
You: After hearing that Lucy broke and screamed at the old lady.
Lucy: Don’t play with me! I’m talking about this baby inside this carriage!
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.Shock
After saying that she turned around to the carriage and saw that it was empty…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.VeryShock
You: Come to think of it, she stopped hearing the cries of the baby the moment this old lady appeared…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.sad
You: ‘W-What’s going on’ muttered Lucy as she felt a sharp pain in her belly…
Old Lady: Oh my, kids these days… 
Old Lady: tHeY GrOw So FaSt…
You: As the old lady was saying that Lucy saw her twisted smile in the light of the moon…
Old Lady: HeHehehEhhe!
You: Lucy decided to abandon the empty carriage. She passed through the old lady and started running with all her might back to the house.
You: Old lady’s laughter echoed from behind and the only thing louder than it was the beating of Lucy’s heart…
You: After a few minutes she couldn’t run anymore and stopped for a short break. She made sure that no one was behind her and started desperately gasping for air.
???: Honey, what happened?
You: Once again, someone caught her by surprise, but this time it was a younger woman in her thirties.
You: She didn’t know why, but she felt a sense of trust in her.
Lucy: There was that old lady and…{{wi}} She started laughing all of sudden…{{wi}} and the baby…
Young woman: Oh my~ That old hag can be scary. I apologize for her.
Young woman: But you do know that a woman in your state should be straining herself like that, right~?
Lucy: Woman? In my state?
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.Shock
At first she didn’t know what the woman meant by that, but one look at her belly made her tremble in fear more than anytime in her life…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.VeryShock
You: Lucy’s belly became swollen and as she was touching it, trying to figure out what’s wrong with her, she felt a kick coming from inside…
Lucy: No! {{punch}}
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.sad
You: Lucy screamed at the top of her lungs and with tears in her eyes started running again.
Young woman: Honey~ Calm down! Think of the baby!
You: Lucy’s heart was beating so loud she couldn’t even hear her own footsteps.
You: When she finally got to the house she made a morbid discovery that her belly grew in size again. She decided to not waste any more time. She grabbed the shotgun and sprinted to the car.
You: She was begging for it to start up and it did. She drove away as fast as possible, leaving a cloud of dust behind her.
You: There was a long road before her, but she couldn’t regain composure. She could feel a sharp, periodic pain in her belly and she instinctively knew what it meant, even though it was impossible…
You: Because of the tears coming out of her eyes and panic, at some point she lost control of the car and crashed.
You: She woke up in the hospital bed. She didn’t remember how she got there, but one touch of her belly made her cry in relief. It was back to normal, like it all was just a bad dream.
You: A nurse came to her and comforted her, but the nurse said one sentence too much…
You: You don’t need to worry! Your baby is fine and well! The nurse said.
That broke Lucy which resulted in months of psychiatric therapy.
You: The doctor explained to her that everything she experienced near her grandfather’s house was just a temporary psychosis caused by a shock of hidden pregnancy. 
You: Hidden pregnancies that reveal themselves at the last moments before birth are rare, but not unheard of.
You: When Lucy finally accepted her circumstances, the doctor allowed her to meet her baby.
You: One look in the eyes of the baby was enough for Lucy to remember the old lady, they had the same, dark, empty eyes…
You: Lucy, with a smile on her face, turned to the doctor and said ‘Thank you, I’m much better now’!
You: What happened next was too gruesome to describe with words…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.VeryShock
You: Lucy attacked the baby she didn’t consider hers in such a brutal manner that even with doctors and nurses at the site its life couldn’t be saved…
#bot.Expression.clear
#bot.Expression.Sad
Bot: What?
Bot: What was the truth then? Was Lucy’s story real, or did she just hallucinate all of it?
You: Who knows? 
#bot.Expression.clear
Bot: I think it’s obvious that it was all a hallucination. That story was not as scary as the previous one.
#bot.Expression.VeryShock
You: If you are so sure it was a hallucination, how about we also rent a car and drive there? It’s a long road, but I know the address of her grandfather’s house.
Bot: T-That won’t be needed!
